source.title: Algebraic relations among special gamma values and the Chowla–Selberg phenomenon over function fields

Independent review: Codex codex-a71f92 read the complete published open-access article, pp.815–897, §§1–7 and bibliography; disputed formulas compared with arXiv v2 PDF and CS-v2.tex. Earlier paywall claim withdrawn.
Published PDF https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00222-026-01406-8.pdf; sha256 5166033945ef2094d03a7ee897c980ec518bc100655117277538d43842f62b2c. CC BY 4.0, published 23 January 2026.

arXiv v2 PDF sha256 7bc90192f53212daa484e0aa6ed07fad68ad9f117470df09471872a3e1460a65; source archive sha256 8b5cef6bf94bb297d1c633f4b0226bc08c032bf3e704fcce8dcd3b8a59520a4a. Published locators control, including Lemma 4.2.6, Corollary 4.2.10, Proposition 5.2.5 and Proposition 7.2.6.

2026-09-23 correction search: journal article/correction links, arXiv version history (v1 and v2), https://www.math.nthu.edu.tw/~ftwei/, and title/DOI searches with erratum/correction. No correction found in these checks; not a claim that none exists.

Primary prerequisite spot-check: ABP, Annals 160 (2004), https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v160-n1-p06.pdf, p.240, Theorem 1.3.2 and definition of E. Other prerequisite papers identified, not independently read in full.

summary: Wei relates characteristic-p gamma values to CM dual t-motive periods through Stickelberger distributions, proves a transcendence-degree formula and Chowla–Selberg formulas, and treats algebraic eigenperiods of CM Hodge–Pink substructures. Independent review requires revision: omitted formulas and hypotheses, confused sigma-dual and contravariant tau-motives, and a special CM transcendence theorem mislabeled as planned by a generic criterion, alongside source boundary errors. This corrected partial inventory does not certify closure. Source routes 2 and 3 are narrowed; proposed Part II route 1 is withheld.

items.name: Polynomial and rational-function carriers
items.statement: For a finite field F_q, A=F_q[θ] and k=F_q(θ); A_+ consists of monic polynomials. Laurent series give the algebraic carrier F_q((1/θ)). This item does not assert the analytic construction or algebraic closedness of C_∞.
items.note: Independent review: Read all cited declarations at Mathlib 082e2d3. Normed C_∞ assembly split into item 85.

items.name: The arithmetic gamma function
items.statement: For y ∈ Z_p with q-adic digits y = Σ_{i≥0} y_i q^i, 0 ≤ y_i < q, set Π_ari(y) = ∏_{i≥1} (∏_{j=0}^{i-1}(1 - θ^{q^j}/θ^{q^i}))^{y_i} and Γ_ari(y) = Π_ari(y-1).
items.note: Goss's arithmetic gamma function, interpolating the Carlitz factorial p-adically. No layer of the atlas plans a gamma function in characteristic p.

items.name: The geometric gamma function
items.note: Thakur's geometric gamma function. The product converges in C_∞; it is the function-field analogue of Euler's product for 1/Γ.

items.name: The two-variable gamma function
items.statement: For x ∈ C_∞ \ (-A_+ ∪ {0}) and y ∈ Z_p with digits y_i, Π_geo(x,y) = ∏_{i≥0} ∏_{a ∈ A_+, deg a = i} (1 + x/a)^{-y_i} and Γ(x,y) = Π_geo(x,y-1)/(x·Π_ari(y-1)). It extends both the arithmetic and the geometric gamma functions: Γ(x, 1 - 1/(q-1))·Γ_ari(1 - 1/(q-1)) = Γ_geo(x) for every admissible x.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), §1.1, following Thakur's Γ2 in Definition 8.1.1 of his paper; compared with Goss's original definition in Remark 5.4.1
items.note: The object whose special values the paper's first main theorem is about; Remark 5.4.1 records the comparison with Goss's normalisation.

items.name: The Carlitz fundamental period
items.statement: Fix a (q−1)-st root of −θ. The Carlitz fundamental period is π-tilde=(−θ)^{q/(q−1)}∏_{i≥1}(1−θ^{1−q^i})^{-1}, with period lattice A·π-tilde.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Remark 3.1.8 and the remark after Theorem 1.1.1
items.note: Independent review: DM.0/DM.2 own this. The gamma comparison is item 86, not automatically supplied.

items.name: The second variable: 𝔸 = F_q[t], 𝕜, and the evaluation map v_θ
items.statement: 𝔸 = F_q[t] is the polynomial ring in a variable t transcendental over C_∞, 𝕜 = F_q(t) its fraction field, regarded as the function field of P^1 over F_q, and v_θ: 𝕜 → k the F_q-algebra isomorphism t ↦ θ, corresponding to evaluation at the point θ ∈ P^1(C_∞); one writes f(θ) = v_θ(f).
items.note: Independent review: the polynomial/rational-function carriers are library infrastructure (1); only the chosen-variable/evaluation comparison is recorded here. Import the rational-function algebra API rather than creating a second field theory; exact map declarations remain a closure gap.

items.name: Finite function-field extensions and decomposition groups
items.statement: For a finite separable extension of F_q(t), choose a place over infinity and form its decomposition and inertia groups. For F_{q^ℓ}(t)/F_q(t), ℓ≥1, the Galois group is cyclic generated by q-power Frobenius.
items.note: Independent review: Narrowed to FA.3's finite-extension contract; compatible separable-closure assembly is item 91. Import existing finite-extension infrastructure.

items.name: Lang–Rohrlich analogue: the transcendence degree of gamma values (Theorem 1.1.1 = Theorem 5.4.7)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+ and ℓ ≥ 1, trdeg_{k-bar} k-bar(Γ_geo(x), Γ_ari(y), Γ(x,y) : x ∈ (1/𝔫(θ))A \ (-A_+ ∪ {0}), y ∈ (1/(q^ℓ-1))Z) = 1 + (ℓ - 1/(q-1)^{ε_𝔫})·#(A/𝔫)^×, where ε_𝔫 = 1 if deg 𝔫 > 0 and 0 otherwise.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.1.1, proved as Theorem 5.4.7
items.note: Independent review: Printed main trdeg formula retained as target, NOT declared disproved. E5–E7 invalidate parts of the finite-level proof at q=2, ℓ=1; repairing distributions/field generation is a readiness gate.

items.name: All algebraic relations among gamma values are monomial (Corollary 5.4.8)
items.statement: Every algebraic relation among the values Γ_geo(x), Γ_ari(y) and Γ(x,y), for x ∈ k \ (-A_+ ∪ {0}) and y ∈ Z_(p), is explained by the monomial relations of Proposition 5.4.2, that is by the reflection, multiplication and translation formulas of the three gamma functions.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Corollary 5.4.8, stated in the introduction as the second half of Theorem 1.1.1
items.note: Independent review: x belongs to arithmetic k, not motivic 𝕜. Completeness of relations does not mean every polynomial relation is itself a monomial; retain root extraction/radical closure.

items.name: The period distribution (Theorem 1.2.1 = Theorem 3.3.1)
items.statement: Fix an embedding ν: 𝕜^sep ↪ k-bar extending v_θ. There is a unique Q-linear map 𝒫_ν: 𝒮(𝔊) → C_∞^×/k-bar^× such that 𝒫_ν(φ_{𝕂,Φ^0}) = 𝒫_𝕂(ξ_ν, Φ^0) for every CM field 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕜^sep fixed by the commutator subgroup [𝔊,𝔊_∞] and every Φ^0 ∈ I_𝕂^0, where ξ_ν ∈ J_𝕂 is the point with ν_{ξ_ν} = ν restricted to 𝕂.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.2.1, proved as Theorem 3.3.1
items.note: Independent review: Uniquely divisible quotient C_∞×/k-bar× and representative-independent field generation are prerequisites, not supplied by generic field definitions.

items.name: Gamma distributions come from the period distribution (Theorem 1.2.2 = Theorem 5.4.5)
items.statement: Let ν_1: 𝕂^cyc ↪ C_∞ be the specific embedding of (5.1.1) and 𝒫^cyc_{ν_1} the restriction of the period distribution to 𝒮(𝔊^cyc). Then Γ-hat_geo = 𝒫^cyc_{ν_1} ∘ St^geo, Γ-hat_ari = 𝒫^cyc_{ν_1} ∘ St^ari and Γ-hat = 𝒫^cyc_{ν_1} ∘ St.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.2.2, proved as Theorem 5.4.5
items.note: Independent review: E7 distinguishes the inconsistent q=2 definition from the independent piecewise normalization. Split the three distributions; gate this target on repair.

items.name: Thakur's conjecture: the Chowla–Selberg phenomenon for CM Drinfeld periods (Theorem 1.2.4 = Theorem 6.2.3)
items.statement: Let 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕂^cyc be an imaginary field over 𝕜 and φ_𝕂 ∈ 𝒮(𝔊^cyc) the characteristic function of Gal(𝕂^cyc/𝕂); write φ_𝕂 = Σ_{x ∈ k/A} Σ_{y ∈ Z_(p)/Z} m_{x,y} St(x,y) with m_{x,y} ∈ Q almost all zero. Then for every nonzero period λ of a Drinfeld 𝔸-module of rank [𝕂:𝕜] over k-bar with CM by O_𝕂, λ ~ ∏_{x} ∏_{y} Γ-tilde(x,y)^{m_{x,y}}.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.2.4, proved as Theorem 6.2.3
items.note: This is the recipe Thakur proposed in 7.12 of his 1991 paper and verified in several cases; it is proved here in general. Because any CM Drinfeld module over k-bar is isogenous to one with CM by the maximal order, the statement applies to every 𝔸-order in 𝕂.

items.name: Chowla–Selberg formula for quasi-periods of CM abelian t-modules (Theorem 1.3.1 = Theorem 6.3.7(1))
items.statement: Let E_ρ be a CM abelian t-module with generalized CM type (𝕂,Ξ) over k-bar, with 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕂_{𝔫,ℓ}, and 𝔥_𝕂 = Gal(𝕂^cyc/𝕂). Write φ_{𝕂,Ξ} for the Stickelberger function of (𝕂,Ξ), viewed as a Z-valued function on 𝔊_𝕂 = Gal(𝕂/𝕜), and m_ϱ = φ_{𝕂,Ξ}(ϱ). Then the space of quasi-periods of E_ρ is spanned over k-bar by the elements π-tilde^{wt(Ξ)/[𝕂:𝕂^+]} · ∏_{ϱ ∈ 𝔊_𝕂} (∏_{𝔠 | 𝔫} ∏_{a ∈ (𝔸/𝔠)^×, i ∈ Z/ℓZ} Γ-tilde(a(θ)/𝔠(θ), q^i/(1-q^ℓ))^{n_𝔠(ϱϱ_0,a,i)})^{m_ϱ/[𝕂:𝕜]}, one for each ϱ_0 ∈ 𝔊_𝕂, where n_𝔠(ϱ,a,i) is the rational number defined in §6.3.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.3.1, proved as part (1) of Theorem 6.3.7
items.note: The generalisation of Thakur's recipe from periods of CM Drinfeld modules to quasi-periods of CM abelian t-modules with an arbitrary generalized CM type, in the fully explicit form. The abstract form, with the exponents given by any preimage of φ_{𝕂,Ξ} under St, is Theorem 6.1.4.

items.name: Period vectors of CM Hilbert–Blumenthal t-modules (Theorem 1.3.2 = Theorem 6.2.2, explicit in Theorem 6.3.7(2))
items.statement: Let K⊂K_{n,ℓ} be CM, ℓ≥1, d=[K⁺:𝕜], Ξ=ξ₁+⋯+ξ_d a weight-one CM type, and E_ρ a CM abelian t-module of this type over k-bar. Choose ρ_i with ν₁∘ρ_i|K=ν_{ξ_i}. There exist a∈𝒜^cyc_{n,ℓ,Q}, an ideal I_ρ of O_K and a k-bar-linear isomorphism Lie(E_ρ)≅k-bar^d such that the image of Λ_ρ is { (ν_{ξ₁}(α)Γ-tilde(ρ₁★a), …, ν_{ξ_d}(α)Γ-tilde(ρ_d★a)) : α∈I_ρ }. Choose St(a)=φ_{K,Ξ}; Γ-tilde(a) uses its rational coefficients as exponents.
items.locator: Published Theorem 6.2.2, pp.871–872; introduction Theorem 1.3.2 is instead Theorem 6.3.7(2).
items.note: Independent review: Ideal-parametrized lattice and Galois translates restored. Fixed-level existence of a is gated by E6.

items.name: The Deligne–Gross period conjecture for CM Hodge–Pink structures (Theorem 1.4.1 = Theorem 7.3.1)
items.statement: Let M be a pure uniformizable dual t-motive over k-bar and H'⊂H(M) a Hodge–Pink substructure with full CM by K⊂K_{n,ℓ}, ℓ≥1. Choose rational ε(x,y) with φ_{K,Φ_H'}=Σ ε(x,y)St(x,y), for x∈n(θ)^{-1}A/A, y∈(q^ℓ−1)^{-1}Z/Z. For ρ∈G_{n,ℓ}, let ω_ρ be a nonzero ν₁∘ρ|K eigendifferential in H'_C∞∩H_dR(M,k-bar), identifying the subspace via the period isomorphism. If γ∈H_Betti(M) and ∫_γω_ρ≠0, then ∫_γω_ρ ~ ∏ Γ-tilde(x,y)^{ε(ρ^{-1}★x,ρ^{-1}★y)}.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 1.4.1, proved as Theorem 7.3.1
items.note: Independent review: Overview of 77, not a second target. Algebraicity, eigencharacter and nonzero pairing restored.

items.name: Dual t-motives
items.statement: Let L⊂C_∞ be algebraically closed and contain k-bar. In L[t,σ], t is central and σc=c^{1/q}σ. A dual t-motive is a left module finite free over L[t] and L[σ], satisfying (t−θ)^N M⊂σM for some N≥0. Morphisms are L[t,σ]-linear.
items.note: Independent review: DM.4 constructs Hom_Fq(E,G_a) with q-Frobenius τ. Contravariance is not the inverse-Frobenius σ-convention. Import/duality bridge required; do not independently rebuild DM.4/DM.8.

items.name: Isogenies of dual t-motives
items.statement: Over the algebraically closed scalar field L of item 16, an isogeny f:M→M' is injective with finite-dimensional L-cokernel. There are nonzero a∈F_q[t] and an isogeny g:M'→M with f∘g=a·id and g∘f=a·id.
items.note: Independent review: Nonzero a restored. DM.5's Drinfeld Tate theorem over finitely generated fields is not this general σ-dual isogeny calculus.

items.name: The Tate algebra, Frobenius twists and the Betti module
items.statement: T is the Tate algebra of Σ c_i t^i ∈ C_∞[[t]] with |c_i|_∞ → 0; the q^n-power Frobenius twist is f^{(n)} = Σ c_i^{q^n} t^i, giving T a C_∞[t,σ]-module structure with σ·f = f^{(-1)}. For a dual t-motive 𝕄 put M = T ⊗_{𝕂[t]} 𝕄; the Betti module is H_Betti(𝕄) = M^σ. It is free over 𝔸 of rank at most rank_{𝕂[t]}𝕄 and T ⊗_𝔸 H_Betti(𝕄) → M is injective.
items.note: Independent review: Tate carrier already exists: item 87. Frobenius, Betti fixed points, finiteness and comparison map remain and must be split.

items.name: Uniformizability
items.statement: A dual t-motive 𝕄 is uniformizable if T ⊗_𝔸 H_Betti(𝕄) → M is surjective, hence an isomorphism of T[σ]-modules; then rank_𝔸 H_Betti(𝕄) = rank_{𝕂[t]}𝕄 and H_Betti(𝕄) ⊂ T^† ⊗_{𝕂[t]} 𝕄, where T^† ⊂ T is the subring of rigid analytic functions on C_∞ \ {θ^{q^i} : i ∈ N}.
items.note: Independent review: Uniformizability is a DM.4 topic, but this bundle's σ-dual Betti comparison and dagger extension need a checked bridge and separate items.

items.name: Push-forward of a morphism on Betti modules
items.statement: Assume the scalar field 𝕂⊂C_∞ is algebraically closed and contains k-bar. For uniformizable 𝕄, 𝕄' over 𝕂 and a morphism f, extending f to M → M' induces f_*: H_Betti(𝕄) → H_Betti(𝕄'). If f is an isogeny then f_* is injective and dim_{F_q}(H_Betti(𝕄')/f_*H_Betti(𝕄)) = dim_𝕂(𝕄'/f(𝕄)) < ∞, so id ⊗ f_* is an isomorphism after tensoring with 𝕜.
items.note: The compatibility that lets periods be compared across an isogeny, which is what makes the period symbol depend only on the CM type.

items.name: Morphisms over C_infinity are defined over the field of definition (Lemma 2.2.7)
items.statement: Assume the scalar field 𝕂⊂C_∞ is algebraically closed and contains k-bar. Let 𝕄, 𝕄' be uniformizable dual t-motives over 𝕂 and 𝕄_{C_∞}, 𝕄'_{C_∞} their base changes. Then every morphism 𝕄_{C_∞} → 𝕄'_{C_∞} over C_∞ already satisfies f(𝕄) ⊆ 𝕄', i.e. is defined over 𝕂.
items.note: Independent review: Ambient §2.1 algebraic-closedness restored; needed for descent. E15 concerns matrix shapes, not the lemma.

items.name: Purity and the weight of a dual t-motive
items.statement: Extend σ to 𝕄((1/t)) = 𝕂((1/t)) ⊗_{𝕂[t]} 𝕄 by σ(f ⊗ m) = f^{(-1)} ⊗ σm. 𝕄 is pure if there are a 𝕂[[1/t]]-lattice L of 𝕄((1/t)) and u,v ∈ N with t^u L = σ^v L; then -u/v = -rank_{𝕂[σ]}𝕄 / rank_{𝕂[t]}𝕄 =: w(𝕄), the weight. Any subquotient of a pure dual t-motive is pure of the same weight.
items.note: Independent review: DM.4 already includes purity. Import its owner; reconcile the inverse-Frobenius weight convention and separate subquotient theorem before marking the bundle planned.

items.name: CM fields over 𝕜, the set J_𝕂 and generalized CM types
items.statement: A CM field K/𝕜 is finite separable with every place over infinity in its maximal totally real subfield K⁺ nonsplit in K; totally real means infinity splits completely. Base-change its smooth projective curve from F_q to k-bar. J_K is the set of points over t=θ; I_K is free abelian on J_K. I_K⁰ consists of Σm_ξξ whose sums over fibres to J_{K⁺} are constant, called wt. A generalized CM type is a NONZERO effective element of I_K⁰; weight one defines a CM type.
items.note: The function-field notion of a CM type, allowing multiplicities and weights, which is what makes the theory cover quasi-periods and not only periods. No layer of the atlas plans CM theory for t-motives.

items.name: J_𝕂 parametrises the embeddings of 𝕂 into C_infinity (Remark 2.3.3)
items.statement: Let Emb(𝕂,C_∞) be the embeddings ν: 𝕂 ↪ C_∞ restricting to ν_θ on 𝕜. Then ξ ↦ ν_ξ is a bijection J_𝕂 → Emb(𝕂,C_∞), where ξ corresponds to an F_q-morphism Spec(C_∞) → X that is not F_q-bar-valued.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Remark 2.3.3, after Proposition 3.3.4 of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei
items.note: The dictionary that turns a CM type, a divisor on J_𝕂, into a set of embeddings with multiplicities, so that a period symbol can be indexed by an embedding.

items.name: Inflation and restriction of CM types
items.statement: For CM fields 𝕂_1 ⊂ 𝕂_2 over 𝕜 with associated morphism π: X_2 → X_1, Inf_{𝕂_2/𝕂_1} = π^* and Res_{𝕂_2/𝕂_1} = π_* carry I^0 into I^0, hence carry generalized CM types to generalized CM types.
items.note: The functoriality that makes the period symbol and the Stickelberger function independent of the field in which a CM type is considered (Lemma 3.2.11).

items.name: CM dual t-motives
items.statement: Use L for the algebraically closed scalar field, K/𝕜 for the CM field. A CM dual t-motive M over L has [K:𝕜]=rank_{L[t]}M; an action O_K→End_{L[t,σ]}(M) making M projective of rank one over L⊗_{F_q}O_K; a nonzero effective Ξ∈I_K⁰ with σM=I_ΞM, where I_Ξ=∏P_ξ^{m_ξ}; and purity. Its generalized CM type is (K,Ξ).
items.locator: Published Definition 2.4.1, p.831; σ corrects E14.
items.note: Remark 2.4.2 records that this axiomatic definition agrees with the geometric one of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei, built after Sinha, Brownawell–Papanikolas and Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas.

items.name: Existence, uniformizability and isogeny of CM dual t-motives (Theorem 2.4.3)
items.statement: Over the algebraically closed scalar field L⊂C_∞ containing k-bar: (1) For every CM field 𝕂 and every generalized CM type Ξ of 𝕂 there is a CM dual t-motive with generalized CM type (𝕂,Ξ) over k-bar. (2) Every CM dual t-motive is uniformizable and pure. (3) Two CM dual t-motives over 𝕂 with the same generalized CM type are isogenous over 𝕂.
items.note: Quoted from Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei. Part (3) with the push-forward of §2.2.6 is what makes the period symbol depend only on (𝕂,Ξ).

items.name: De Rham realisation and quasi-periods of a dual t-motive
items.statement: For uniformizable M over algebraically closed L, H_dR(M,L)=Hom_L(M/(t−θ)M,L). Extend ω to γ∈(T⊗M)^σ by f⊗m↦f(θ)ω(m); the dagger extension makes evaluation meaningful and defines ∫_γω. The C_∞-linear period comparison is an isomorphism. For CM M, the ξ-eigenline is one-dimensional; choose a NONZERO ω_{M,ξ} therein.
items.note: The de Rham side of the period pairing for dual t-motives, in the form of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei §5; DM.2 plans periods of Drinfeld modules through analytic uniformization but not the de Rham module of a dual t-motive.

items.name: Essentially surjective morphisms
items.statement: A morphism f: 𝕄 → 𝕄' of uniformizable dual t-motives over 𝕂 is essentially surjective if f(𝕄) is isogenous to 𝕄' via the inclusion; then f_*^∨ and hence f^*: H_dR(𝕄',𝕂) → H_dR(𝕄,𝕂) are injective.
items.note: The notion in which the Hodge–Pink comparison of §7 is stated: a Hodge–Pink sub-structure is realised by an essentially surjective morphism of dual t-motives, not by a sub-object.

items.name: Period symbols
items.statement: For a CM field 𝕂 over 𝕜, a generalized CM type Ξ and ξ ∈ J_𝕂, the period symbol 𝒫_𝕂(ξ,Ξ) is the class in C_∞^×/k-bar^× of ∫_γ ω_{𝕄,ξ} for any CM dual t-motive 𝕄 with generalized CM type (𝕂,Ξ) over k-bar and any nonzero γ ∈ H_Betti(𝕄); p_𝕂(ξ,Ξ) denotes a representative.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Definition 3.1.7, following Definition 5.2.2 of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei
items.note: The function-field analogue of Shimura's period symbols. Well-definedness rests on Theorem 2.4.3(3) and the push-forward of §2.2.6.

items.name: The period symbol as a homomorphism, with the Legendre relation (Theorem 3.1.9)
items.statement: For each ξ ∈ J_𝕂, 𝒫_𝕂(ξ,·) extends uniquely to a group homomorphism I_𝕂^0 → C_∞^×/k-bar^× satisfying: (1) 𝒫_𝕂(Res_{𝕂'/𝕂}(ξ'),Φ^0) = 𝒫_{𝕂'}(ξ', Inf_{𝕂'/𝕂}(Φ^0)); (2) 𝒫_𝕂(ξ^ϱ, Φ^0) = 𝒫_𝕂(ξ, (Φ^0)^{ϱ^{-1}}) for ϱ ∈ Aut(𝕂/𝕜); and (3) the Legendre relation ∏_{ξ ↦ ξ^+} p_𝕂(ξ,Φ^0) ~ π-tilde^{wt(Φ^0)} for every ξ^+ ∈ J_{𝕂^+}.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 3.1.9, from Theorem 1.3.1, equivalently Theorem 5.3.2, of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei
items.note: These three properties are exactly what a distribution on the Galois group needs, and they are the reason the period distribution of Theorem 3.3.1 exists.

items.name: Stickelberger functions
items.statement: 𝒮(𝔊) is the space of locally constant Q-valued functions φ on 𝔊 such that (1) φ(ϱ_1 · (ϱ_2 ϱ_∞ ϱ_2^{-1} ϱ_∞^{-1})) = φ(ϱ_1) for all ϱ_1, ϱ_2 ∈ 𝔊 and ϱ_∞ ∈ 𝔊_∞, and (2) ∫_{𝔊_∞} φ(ϱ_1 ϱ_∞) dϱ_∞ is independent of ϱ_1, for the normalised Haar measure on 𝔊_∞.
items.note: Mathlib has locally constant functions and the Haar measure of a compact group, so the carrier is available, but the space cut out by these two conditions — the function-field analogue of the space on which Stickelberger elements live — is not planned anywhere.

items.name: The 𝔊-action on 𝒮(𝔊), stabilisers and the associated CM field
items.statement: 𝒮(𝔊) carries the left 𝔊-action (ϱ_0 · φ)(ϱ) = φ(ϱϱ_0). For φ ∈ 𝒮(𝔊) the stabiliser 𝔥_φ has finite index, its fixed field 𝕂_φ is a CM field over 𝕜 whose fixing subgroup contains [𝔊,𝔊_∞], and 𝔥_{𝕂_φ} = 𝔥_φ.
items.note: This is what turns an abstract Stickelberger function into CM data, and is the mechanism behind the isomorphism of Remark 3.2.12.

items.name: The Stickelberger function attached to a CM type
items.statement: Fix ν extending v_θ. For K fixed by [G,G_∞], H_K=Gal(𝕜^sep/K), and Φ=Σm_ξξ∈I_K⁰, choose ρ_ξ with ν∘ρ_ξ|K=ν_ξ. Set φ_{K,Φ}=Σm_ξ·1_{ρ_ξH_K}. This is independent of representatives and lies in S(G).
items.note: The bridge between CM types and Stickelberger functions on which everything after §3 is built.

items.name: 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂) is the rational span of the CM types (Lemma 3.2.9)
items.statement: Let 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕜^sep be a CM field with 𝔥_𝕂 ⊇ [𝔊,𝔊_∞]. (1) φ_{𝕂,Φ^0} ∈ 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂) for every Φ^0 ∈ I_𝕂^0, and Φ^0 ↦ φ_{𝕂,Φ^0} is injective. (2) 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂) consists of the rational multiples of these, so φ_𝕂 induces a Q-linear isomorphism Q ⊗_Z I_𝕂^0 ≅ 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 3.2.9, with the dimension formula dim_Q 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂) = 1 + (1 - 1/[𝕂:𝕂^+])[𝕂:𝕜] of Remark 3.2.10
items.note: The finite-level identification of Stickelberger functions with CM types, which converts the transcendence statement of Theorem 3.3.5 into a dimension count.

items.name: Compatibility of Stickelberger functions with inflation (Lemma 3.2.11)
items.statement: For CM fields 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕂' over 𝕜 fixed by [𝔊,𝔊_∞] and Φ^0 ∈ I_𝕂^0, one has φ_{𝕂,Φ^0} = φ_{𝕂', Inf_{𝕂'/𝕂}(Φ^0)} in 𝒮(𝔊). Consequently 𝒮(𝔊) is the colimit of the 𝒮(𝔊/𝔥_𝕂) and is spanned by the φ_{𝕂,Ξ}.
items.note: The compatibility that lets the period distribution be defined on all of 𝒮(𝔊) at once rather than level by level.

items.name: Transcendence degree of the period distribution and its injectivity (Theorem 3.3.5)
items.statement: Let 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕜^sep be a CM field Galois over 𝕜 and fixed by [𝔊,𝔊_∞], with maximal totally real subfield 𝕂^+. Then trdeg_{k-bar} k-bar(𝒫_ν(𝒮(𝔊_𝕂))) = 1 + (1 - 1/[𝕂:𝕂^+])·[𝕂:𝕜]. Consequently 𝒫_ν: 𝒮(𝔊) → C_∞^×/k-bar^× is injective.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 3.3.5, resting on the main theorem of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei on Shimura's conjecture
items.note: The transcendence input of the whole paper. It is the function-field analogue of Shimura's conjecture on CM periods, proved by Papanikolas-style Tannakian methods; DM.8 plans that machinery but not this theorem.

items.name: Carlitz cyclotomic fields and constant extensions
items.statement: For monic n∈F_q[t], K_n is the splitting field of the Carlitz n-division polynomial, K_{n,ℓ}=F_{q^ℓ}K_n, ℓ≥1. The Artin identification Gal(K_{n,ℓ}/𝕜)≅(F_q[t]/n)××Z/ℓZ sends (a,c) to Carlitz multiplication by a on torsion and q^c-Frobenius on constants. Their compositum is K^cyc. The geometric maximal-real index is (q−1)^{ε_n}, where ε_n=1 for deg n>0, otherwise 0.
items.note: Independent review: Only the later Carlitz ray-class comparison, importing DM.0/DM.1 torsion, not input to reciprocity. S/P restrictions moved to 92; unit modulus corrected by E12.

items.name: The geometric, arithmetic and two-variable diamond brackets
items.statement: For x=Σ_i ε_iθ^{-i}∈k_∞, define ⟨x⟩_N=1 precisely when ε_i=0 for 0<i<N+1 and ε_{N+1}=1, otherwise 0. Set ⟨x⟩_geo=Σ_{N≥0}⟨x⟩_N. Write {x} for its representative modulo A with norm <1, and ⟨y⟩_ari for the ordinary fractional part of y∈Z_(p). For ℓ≥1 with q^ℓ>2 and (q^ℓ−1)y∈Z, write ⟨y⟩_ari=Σ_{i<ℓ}y_i q^i/(q^ℓ−1), 0≤y_i<q; define ⟨x,y⟩=Σ_{i<ℓ} y_i Σ_{N≥0,N≡−1−i mod ℓ}⟨x⟩_N. Independence under nondegenerate refinements is the construction to prove.
items.note: Independent review: Formula restored. E5 prevents imposing the printed degenerate seed at q=2,ℓ=1; the displayed definition is a repaired construction, not a claim that all printed relations survive.

items.name: Digit expansion of the arithmetic bracket (Lemma 4.1.2)
items.statement: For y∈Z_(p), ℓ≥1 and (q^ℓ−1)y∈Z, there are unique 0≤y_i<q with ⟨y⟩_ari=Σ_{i<ℓ}y_i q^i/(q^ℓ−1), using unbracketed fractions. Put wt₀^ari(y)=ℓ^{-1}Σ_i y_i. Then Σ_{i<ℓ}⟨q^i y⟩_ari=ℓ·wt₀^ari(y)/(q−1).
items.note: Independent review: Corrected E5 by using the unbracketed expansion printed immediately before the lemma; removed invented description of part (2).

items.name: Reflection and multiplication formulas for the geometric bracket (Lemma 4.1.4)
items.statement: For x∈k/A and n∈A_+, Σ_{ε∈F_q×}⟨εx⟩_geo=1 if x≠0, otherwise 0; and Σ_{a∈A,deg a<deg n}⟨x+a/n⟩_geo=⟨nx⟩_geo+(q^{deg n}−1)/(q−1).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 4.1.4, compare 5.5.5 of Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas
items.note: The geometric counterpart of Lemma 4.1.2; together they generate all the relations among gamma values.

items.name: Characterisation of the two-variable bracket (Proposition 4.1.5)
items.statement: With nondegenerate seeds q^ℓ>2, the two-variable bracket of item 39 is periodic under (x,y)↦(x+a,y+N), for a∈A,N∈Z, linear in the canonical digits of ⟨y⟩_ari, and satisfies ⟨x,q^i/(q^ℓ−1)⟩=Σ_{N≥0,N≡−1−i mod ℓ}⟨x⟩_N for 0≤i<ℓ. These conditions define it uniquely. The printed assertion including q=2,ℓ=1 is inconsistent (E5).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Proposition 4.1.5, with Remark 4.1.6 comparing Thakur's Definition 8.3.1
items.note: The two-variable bracket is characterised rather than constructed, which is what makes the verification of its relations a finite check.

items.name: Relations for the two-variable bracket (Proposition 4.1.7 and Remark 4.1.8)
items.statement: For q^ℓ>2, |x|_∞<1 and 0≤i<ℓ, Σ_{ε∈F_q×}⟨εx,q^i/(q^ℓ−1)⟩ is 1 when x≠0 and ord_∞x≡−i mod ℓ, otherwise 0. For x∈k,y∈Z_(p), ⟨x,y⟩+⟨x,−y⟩=(q−1)⟨x⟩_geo if y∉Z, otherwise 0. For monic n, Σ_{deg a<deg n}(⟨(x+a)/n,y⟩−⟨a/n,y⟩)=⟨x,q^{deg n}y⟩.
items.note: Independent review: Remaining reflection/multiplication reformulations in Remark 4.1.8 need separate items. Do not use the degenerate seed; E5.

items.name: The Stickelberger functions St^geo, St^ari and St
items.statement: For x ∈ k/A and y ∈ Z_(p)/Z, identify k/A with the Carlitz torsion and Z_(p)/Z with roots of unity in k-bar and equip them with the 𝔊-action ★ through the Artin map. Set St^geo(x)(ϱ) = ⟨ϱ★x⟩_geo - 1/(q-1), St^ari(y)(ϱ) = ⟨-ϱ★y⟩_ari and St(x,y)(ϱ) = ⟨ϱ★x, -ϱ★y⟩ - ⟨-ϱ★y⟩_ari. All three lie in 𝒮(𝔊^cyc).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Definition 4.2.2, with the group actions of (4.2.1) and (4.2.2)
items.note: These are the function-field Stickelberger elements, in the sense of Kubert–Lang Chapter 1 §3; the paper's whole strategy is that they are universal distributions.

items.name: Distribution relations for the Stickelberger functions (Remark 4.2.3)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+ and ℓ ∈ N, and x ∈ (1/𝔫(θ))A/A, y ∈ (1/(q^ℓ-1))Z/Z, the maps St^geo, St^ari and St satisfy the distribution relations induced by the diamond bracket relations of §4.1, so they are distributions on k/A, Z_(p)/Z and their product with values in 𝒮(𝔊^cyc).
items.note: The distribution property is what allows the universal-distribution comparison in §4.3.

items.name: The Stickelberger functions span (Proposition 4.2.4)
items.statement: Restrict to q^ℓ>2; the unrestricted printed finite-level statement is false by E6. For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+ and ℓ ∈ N: (1) 𝒮(𝔊_{1,ℓ}) is spanned by St^ari(y) for y ∈ (1/(q^ℓ-1))Z/Z, hence 𝒮(𝔊^ari) by all St^ari(y); (2) 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,1}) is spanned by the St^geo(x); (3) 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}) is spanned by the St(x,y).
items.note: Independent review: Restriction removes the exhibited zero-source counterexample, but is not a certification of the entire repaired proof. Keep the finite-level exceptional constant direction separate from the direct-limit theorem.

items.name: Stickelberger functions evaluate Dirichlet L-values (Lemma 4.2.8)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+, ℓ ∈ N, a character χ of 𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ} and 𝔪 ∈ 𝔸_+ dividing 𝔫, the sum Σ_{ϱ ∈ 𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}} χ-bar(ϱ) St(a(θ)/𝔪(θ), q^c/(1-q^ℓ))(ϱ) equals the stated multiple of the Dirichlet L-value L_𝔸(0,χ-bar), when the finite part χ_f is nontrivial.
items.note: Independent review: Original locator 4.2.8 was a display, not the lemma. Exact two cases remain a gap: use imprimitive L_A^m with its Euler factors and character/shift normalization, not an unspecified multiple of primitive L. E6 also affects the trivial-character constant case.

items.name: When a Dirichlet L-value at 0 vanishes (Corollary 4.2.12)
items.statement: For χ a character of 𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}, L_𝔸(0,χ) = 0 if and only if χ is nontrivial and χ(ϱ_{ε,c}) = 1 for all ε ∈ F_q^× and c ∈ Z/ℓZ.
items.note: Independent review: Checked against the source: the condition includes χ≠1. FA.5 owns these finite-cover Artin factors; this is not the gamma evaluator theorem.

items.name: The universal distributions 𝒰^ari, 𝒰^geo and 𝒰^cyc
items.statement: 𝒜^ari_{ℓ,Q}, 𝒜^geo_{𝔫,Q} and 𝒜^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ,Q} are the Q-vector spaces on the corresponding sets of fractions, and 𝒰^ari_ℓ, 𝒰^geo_𝔫 and 𝒰^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ} are their quotients by the subspaces generated by the diamond-bracket distribution relations — the universal distributions in the sense of Kubert–Lang.
items.note: The universal distribution is the combinatorial object whose dimension has to match the transcendence degree; this is the only place where the paper's argument is purely linear algebra.

items.name: Universality of the arithmetic Stickelberger distribution (Lemma 4.3.1, Lemma 4.3.2, Corollary 4.3.3)
items.statement: Restrict to q^ℓ>2; the unrestricted printed finite-level statement is false by E6. dim_Q 𝒰^ari_ℓ ≤ ℓ for every ℓ; St^ari: 𝒜^ari_{ℓ,Q} → 𝒮(𝔊_{1,ℓ}) is surjective; hence the induced map 𝒰^ari_ℓ → 𝒮(𝔊_{1,ℓ}) is an isomorphism, dim_Q 𝒰^ari_ℓ = dim_Q 𝒮(𝔊_{1,ℓ}) = ℓ, and 𝒰^ari ≅ 𝒮(𝔊^ari).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 4.3.1, Lemma 4.3.2 and Corollary 4.3.3
items.note: Independent review: Restriction removes the exhibited zero-source counterexample, but is not a certification of the entire repaired proof. Keep the finite-level exceptional constant direction separate from the direct-limit theorem.

items.name: Universality of the geometric Stickelberger distribution (Lemma 4.3.5, Lemma 4.3.6, Corollary 4.3.7)
items.statement: dim_Q 𝒰^geo_𝔫 ≤ 1 + (1 - 1/(q-1)^{ε_𝔫})·#(A/𝔫)^×; St^geo: 𝒜^geo_{𝔫,Q} → 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,1}) is surjective; hence 𝒰^geo_𝔫 ≅ 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,1}) with that dimension, and 𝒰^geo ≅ 𝒮(𝔊^geo).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 4.3.5, Lemma 4.3.6 and Corollary 4.3.7
items.note: The geometric analogue, with ε_𝔫 = 1 if deg 𝔫 > 0 and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Universality of the two-variable Stickelberger distribution (Lemma 4.3.11, Lemma 4.3.12, Corollary 4.3.13)
items.statement: Restrict to q^ℓ>2; the unrestricted printed finite-level statement is false by E6. dim_Q 𝒰^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ} ≤ 1 + (ℓ - 1/(q-1)^{ε_𝔫})·#(𝔸/𝔫)^×; St: 𝒜^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ,Q} → 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}) is surjective; hence 𝒰^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ} ≅ 𝒮(𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}) with that dimension, and 𝒰^cyc ≅ 𝒮(𝔊^cyc).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 4.3.11, Lemma 4.3.12 and Corollary 4.3.13, summarised in Remark 4.3.15
items.note: Independent review: Restriction removes the exhibited zero-source counterexample, but is not a certification of the entire repaired proof. Keep the finite-level exceptional constant direction separate from the direct-limit theorem.

items.name: Generalized CM types attached to Stickelberger functions (Lemma 5.1.2)
items.statement: For q>2, ℓ≥1 and the §5.1 divisors over K_{n,ℓ}, the Ξ-divisors are effective and lie in I⁰; they are generalized CM types only when nonzero (Ξ_x requires x≠0, Ξ_y requires y≠0, Ξ_(x,y) requires both). Φ_x=Ξ_x−Ξ_{1/(q−1)} and Φ_(x,y)=Ξ_(x,−y)−Ξ_{−y} lie in I⁰. With denominator D=q^ℓ−1, St₀^geo(x)=φ_{Ξ_x}/D, St^ari(−y)=φ_{Ξ_y}/D, St₀(x,y)=φ_{Ξ_(x,y)}/D, St^geo(x)=φ_{Φ_x}/D, and St(x,y)=φ_{Φ_(x,y)}/D.
items.note: Independent review: Ξ_x, not Φ_x, occurs in the first identity. E8 corrects zero CM types; q>2 isolates E5/E7 rather than claiming a complete q=2 repair. Exact divisor definitions remain to split.

items.name: Shtuka functions for cyclotomic function fields (Theorem 5.2.1)
items.statement: For monic n of positive degree and nonzero x∈n(θ)^{-1}A/A, there is g_x=1+Σc_{ij}t^iz^j in k-bar⊗_{F_q}O_n, |c_{ij}|_∞<1, with div(g_x)=−∞_{X_n}+Σ_{α∈(F_q[t]/n)×}Σ_{N≥0}⟨α(θ)x⟩_N ξ_α^{(N)}, where ∞_{X_n} is the reduced sum of points over infinity.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 5.2.1, from §6.3.9 of Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas
items.note: Independent review: DM.7 constructs elliptic-sheaf chains, not this ABP special function. Import the generic geometry and plan the specific soliton function once; no existing declaration found.

items.name: Divisors of the twisted shtuka products (Proposition 5.2.6)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+, ℓ ∈ N and x, y as above, div(h_x), div(h_y) and div(h_{(x,y)}) are the stated combinations of the infinite point of X_𝔫, the divisors Ξ^#, and the Frobenius twists W^{(ℓ)} - W.
items.note: Independent review: Still a placeholder: three actual divisors, W_*, h_* and component embeddings must be extracted separately. E12 requires a unit-modulus branch.

items.name: Generalized soliton dual t-motives
items.statement: For q>2, deg n>0 and nonzero Ξ_* (x≠0 for *=x, y≠0 for *=y, both for *=(x,y)), the §5.3 divisor construction gives M(*) with σ(m₀,…,m_{ℓ−1})=(h_*m_{ℓ−1}^{(−1)},m₀^{(−1)},…,m_{ℓ−2}^{(−1)}). The convergent product ψ_*=∏_{j≥1}(h_*^{-1})^{(ℓj)} is a unit in the analytic algebra T⊗O_n, extends to the stated dagger algebra, and (ψ_*,ψ_*^{(−1)},…,ψ_*^{(1−ℓ)}) is a Betti cycle.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Lemma 5.3.1, Lemma 5.3.2 and Remark 5.3.3, generalizing 6.4.2 of Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas
items.note: Independent review: The product is not asserted to be an algebraic regular unit. E8 excludes zero-type objects; sheaf-section modules and convergence proof still need separate extraction. Arithmetic/unit-modulus case requires E12 repair.

items.name: The soliton evaluates to a gamma product (Proposition 5.3.4)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+, ℓ ∈ N, nonzero x ∈ (1/𝔫(θ))A with |x|_∞ < 1, and y = q^c/(q^ℓ-1) with 0 ≤ c < ℓ, one has ψ_{(x,y)}(ξ_{1,0}) = ∏_{j≥0} ∏_{a ∈ A_+, deg a = c+ℓj} (1 + x/a)^{1-q^ℓ}.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Proposition 5.3.4, with Remark 5.3.5 for the purely geometric case
items.note: Independent review: Corrected monic index by E9. The separate arithmetic product formula for ψ_y in the same proposition remains to extract.

items.name: Monomial relations among gamma values (Proposition 5.4.2)
items.statement: For x∈C_∞\(−A_+∪{0}) and y∈Z_p, Γ_ari(y)Γ_ari(1−y)~π-tilde and Γ(x,y)Γ(x,1−y)~x^{q−3}Γ_geo(x)^{q−1}/π-tilde. For algebraic x the extra factor is absorbed by ~. This item records only Proposition 5.4.2(1), corrected by E10; parts (2)–(6) remain a closure gap.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Proposition 5.4.2, with Remark 5.4.3 for the geometric specialisation
items.note: Independent review: The old two-line placeholder concealed six parts. Remaining algebraicity, translation, digit, reflection-orbit and multiplication relations are explicitly unextracted, not accepted as a complete presentation.

items.name: The soliton period equals the gamma product (Proposition 5.4.4)
items.statement: For the well-defined §5.3 analytic products (with zero cases defined as empty products), put u={x}, v=⟨y⟩_ari and D=q^ℓ−1. Then ψ_x(ξ₁₀)=Π_geo(u)^D; ψ_y(ξ₁₀)=Π_ari(−v)^D; ψ_(x,y)(ξ₁₀)=Π_geo(u,−v)^D; and ψ_(x,y)(ξ₁₀)/ψ_y(ξ₁₀)=Π(u,−v)^D, where Π(u,z)=Π_geo(u,z)/Π_ari(z).
items.note: Independent review: All four identities are exact; removed 'up to the stated factor'. Separate analytic identities from false zero-type motive claims (E8).

items.name: Abelian Anderson t-modules
items.statement: Over k-bar, an Anderson t-module E_ρ is G_a^d, d≥1, with an F_q-algebra homomorphism ρ:F_q[t]→Mat_d(k-bar[τ]) whose differential at t is θI_d+N with N nilpotent. Its contravariant motive M_ρ=Hom_Fq(E_ρ,G_a) is a k-bar[t,τ]-module; E_ρ is abelian if M_ρ is finitely generated over k-bar[t].
items.note: Independent review: Narrowed to DM.4's actual convention. Hartl–Juschka dual and quasi-period comparison, including the sign, are item 89; Drinfeld-only DM.2 does not supply them.

items.name: Quasi-periods of CM abelian t-modules as gamma monomials (Theorem 6.1.4)
items.statement: Let E_ρ over k-bar have generalized CM type (K,Ξ), with K⊂K_{n,ℓ}, ℓ≥1. Put H_K=Gal(K^cyc/K). Given a∈𝒜^cyc_{n,ℓ,Q} with St(a)=φ_{K,Ξ}, the quasi-period space is span_{k-bar}{Γ-tilde(ρ★a):ρH_K∈G^cyc/H_K}. The paper asserts such a exists at this fixed level; E6 gates that existence.
items.note: Independent review: Restored the whole Galois orbit. One gamma monomial would span only a line, whereas even rank-two Drinfeld examples have a two-dimensional quasi-period space. Source typo E16 is separate.

items.name: Thakur's conjecture (Theorem 6.2.3)
items.statement: Let E_ρ be a Drinfeld 𝔸-module over k-bar with CM by O_𝕂, where 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕂_{𝔫,ℓ} is imaginary and O_𝕂 the integral closure of 𝔸 in 𝕂, and 𝔥_𝕂 = Gal(𝕂^cyc/𝕂). For any 𝕒 ∈ 𝒜^cyc_{𝔫,ℓ,Q} with St(𝕒) = φ_𝕂, every nonzero period λ of E_ρ satisfies λ ~ ∏_{x,y} Γ-tilde(x,y)^{a_{x,y}}. Moreover {Γ-tilde(ρ★a):ρH_K∈G^cyc/H_K} is algebraically independent over k-bar and forms a k-bar-basis of the quasi-period space.
items.note: Independent review: Independence and basis assertion restored. Item 12 is the introductory duplicate; fixed-level existence is gated by E6.

items.name: Stickelberger functions and L-values at a character (Lemma 6.3.2)
items.statement: For χ∈Ĝ_{n,ℓ} with conductor cχ, Σ_{(a,i)∈(F_q[t]/cχ)××Z/ℓZ} conjugate(χ(a,i+deg cχ))·St(a(θ)/cχ(θ),q^i/(1−q^ℓ)) = L_A(0,conjugate χ)·χ as complex-valued functions on G_{n,ℓ}. At q=2,ℓ=1 the printed trivial-character instance fails (E6).
items.note: Independent review: χ is the character function, not an undefined eχ. Complexifying S(G) is required.

items.name: Explicit decomposition of φ_{𝕂,Ξ} (Proposition 6.3.5)
items.statement: For K⊂K_{n,ℓ}, Ξ=Σ_ρm_ρξ_ρ, put n_c(ρ,a,i)=Σ_{χ∈Ĝ_K\Ĝ_{K⁺},cχ=c}χ(ρ)χ(a,i+deg c)/L_A(0,χ)∈Q. For ρ₀∈G_K, φ_{K,Ξ^{ρ₀}}=wt(Ξ)/[K:K⁺]·1+[K:𝕜]^{-1}Σ_{c|n}Σ_{a∈(F_q[t]/c)×,i mod ℓ}(Σ_ρm_ρ n_c(ρρ₀,a,i))St(a(θ)/c(θ),q^i/(1−q^ℓ)).
items.note: Independent review: Restored the twisted type, constant term, character family, conductor and degree normalization. Source small-field gates still apply.

items.name: The explicit Chowla–Selberg formula (Theorem 6.3.7)
items.statement: Let E_ρ be a CM abelian t-module with generalized CM type (𝕂,Ξ) over k-bar, 𝕂 ⊂ 𝕂_{𝔫,ℓ}, 𝔊_𝕂 = Gal(𝕂/𝕜) and Ξ = Σ_{ϱ} m_ϱ ξ_ϱ ∈ I_𝕂^0. Then the quasi-periods of E_ρ are given explicitly by products of the values Γ-tilde(a(θ)/𝔠(θ), q^i/(1-q^ℓ)) with exponents expressed through the m_ϱ and the Dirichlet L-values L_𝔸(0,χ).
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 6.3.7, announced in §1.3 as Theorems 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and 1.3.3
items.note: Independent review: Corrected Γ-tilde argument (raw Γ uses 1−q^i/(q^ℓ−1)). Still non-atomic: exact three targets including lattice and independent basis must be split; 13,14,62 partially supply them, not full closure.

items.name: Chowla–Selberg for constant field extensions (Example 6.3.9)
items.statement: For K=F_{q^ℓ}(t), ℓ≥1, n₁(1,i)=q−1+ℓ·1_{i=0}−ℓq·1_{i=ℓ−1}. For ℓ=1 this is 0, unlike the overlapping printed cases. For a rank-ℓ Drinfeld module with CM by F_{q^ℓ}[t], the source gives λ~Γ_ari(1−q^{ℓ−1}/(q^ℓ−1))^q/Γ_ari(1−1/(q^ℓ−1)) for nonzero periods, and the analogous cyclic ratios indexed by c=0,…,ℓ−1 as an algebraically independent quasi-period basis.
items.note: Independent review: E13 fixes the overlapping character-sum cases. The final raw-gamma period identities are not declared false; their derivation through the degenerate finite-level distribution requires a separate repair.

items.name: Chowla–Selberg for the t-th Carlitz cyclotomic field (Example 6.3.10)
items.statement: For K=𝕜((-t)^{1/(q−1)}) and a rank-(q−1) Drinfeld module with CM by F_q[(-t)^{1/(q−1)}], every nonzero period λ satisfies λ~Γ_geo(1/θ). The family {Γ_geo(ε/θ):ε∈F_q×} is algebraically independent over k-bar and is a basis of its quasi-period space.
items.note: Independent review: Explicit specialization restored. The source's intermediate raw-Γ manipulation at q=2 must not be justified by a nonexistent nonzero arithmetic residue.

items.name: Chowla–Selberg for imaginary quadratic extensions (Example 6.3.11)
items.statement: For imaginary quadratic K⊂K^cyc, conductor/discriminant d, quadratic character χ_K and w_K=#O_K×/#F_q×, define varpi_K^±=π-tilde^{1/2}∏_{a∈(F_q[t]/d)×,i mod 2}Γ-tilde(a(θ)/d(θ),q^i/(1−q²))^{±w_Kχ_K(a,i+deg d)/(2#Pic(O_K))}. For rank-two CM Drinfeld E_ρ, λ~varpi_K^+ for nonzero periods and {varpi_K^+,varpi_K^-} is an algebraically independent quasi-period basis.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Example 6.3.11, with Remark 6.3.13 for the case χ_𝕂(1,i) = 1
items.note: Independent review: Use quotient-normalized Γ-tilde, as in introduction Remark 1.3.4, to include constant quadratic fields (E18). Raw Γ at x=0 is undefined. E3 fixes the omega/varpi name.

items.name: Logarithmic derivative of an arithmetic L-function (Lemma 6.4.2)
items.statement: For ℓ ∈ N and a character χ of 𝔊_{1,ℓ}, L'_𝔸(0,χ) = -Σ_{c=0}^{ℓ-1} χ(c)·ln|Γ^*_ari(1 - q^c/(q^ℓ-1))|_∞, where Γ^*_ari is the normalised arithmetic gamma value.
items.note: The first step of the Lerch-type formula, relating the derivative at 0 of a Dirichlet L-function to logarithms of gamma values.

items.name: A Lerch-type formula (Theorem 6.4.5)
items.statement: For 𝔫 ∈ 𝔸_+, ℓ ∈ N and a character χ of 𝔊_{𝔫,ℓ}, L'_𝔸(0,χ) = -L_𝔸(0,χ) ln|𝔠_χ|_∞ + Σ_{a ∈ 𝔸, deg a < deg 𝔠_χ, gcd(a,𝔠_χ)=1} Σ_{i=0}^{ℓ-1} χ(a, i + deg 𝔠_χ) ln|Γ^*(a(θ)/𝔠_χ(θ), 1 - q^i/(q^ℓ-1))|_∞.
items.note: The function-field analogue of Lerch's formula, obtained by normalising the gamma values so that the ambiguity by k-bar^× is removed on taking absolute values.

items.name: Logarithmic form of the Chowla–Selberg formula (Corollary 6.4.6)
items.statement: For imaginary K⊂K_{n,ℓ}, let n_c(a,i)=n_c(id_K,a,i) as in item 64. Then log|π-tilde·∏_{c|n}∏_{deg a<deg c,gcd(a,c)=1}∏_{i<ℓ}Γ*(a(θ)/c(θ),1−q^i/(q^ℓ−1))^{n_c(a,i)}|_∞ = ζ'_{O_K}(0)/ζ_{O_K}(0)+log|d(O_K/F_q[t])|_∞, where d is the monic discriminant generator.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Corollary 6.4.6, with Remarks 6.4.7 and 6.4.10
items.note: Independent review: Exact Corollary 6.4.6 restored. The Kronecker-limit and stable Taguchi-height consequences in Remarks 6.4.7/6.4.10 are additional missing items.

items.name: Pre-Hodge–Pink and Hodge–Pink structures
items.statement: A finite-dimensional 𝕜-vector space H has an increasing rational weight filtration with dim Gr^W H=dim H. A mixed pre-Hodge–Pink structure is (H,W,q), q a full C_∞[[t−θ]] lattice in C_∞((t−θ))⊗_𝕜H. After the chosen embedding of 𝕜_∞, for every subspace H'_∞⊂H_∞ put W_μH'_∞=H'_∞∩W_μH_∞, q'=q∩(C_∞((t−θ))⊗H'_∞), p'=C_∞[[t−θ]]⊗H'_∞. Local semistability is dim(q'/(q'∩p'))−dim(p'/(q'∩p'))≤Σ_μμ·dim Gr^W_μH'_∞, with equality whenever H'_∞=𝕜_∞⊗W_μH. This defines a Hodge–Pink structure.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Definitions 7.1.1, 7.1.2 and 7.1.4, following Definition 2.2.3 of Hartl–Juschka
items.note: Independent review: Restored finite-jump condition and equality on weight steps. Morphisms preserving both structures, strictness, substructures, Hodge–Pink lattice filtration and weight conversion still need separate items; classical HodgeStructures is not this owner.

items.name: Hodge–Pink sub-structures are realised by dual t-motives (Theorem 7.1.8)
items.statement: Let 𝕄 be a pure uniformizable dual t-motive over C_∞ and 𝕳' a 𝕜-Hodge–Pink sub-structure of 𝕳(𝕄). Then there is a pure uniformizable dual t-motive 𝕄' over C_∞ and an essentially surjective morphism f: 𝕄 → 𝕄' whose associated morphism of Hodge–Pink structures identifies 𝕳(𝕄') with 𝕳'.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 7.1.8, with Remark 7.1.9 on effectiveness
items.note: The function-field counterpart of the fact that a sub-Hodge-structure of the cohomology of a variety is motivated; it is what lets a Hodge–Pink statement be proved by a statement about dual t-motives.

items.name: Full CM Hodge–Pink structures and their Hodge–Pink type
items.statement: A 𝕜-Hodge–Pink structure 𝕳 has full CM by a CM field 𝕂 over 𝕜 if 𝕂 acts on it with [𝕂:𝕜] = dim_𝕜 H; its Hodge–Pink type is Φ_𝕳 = Σ_{ξ ∈ J_𝕂} w_ξ ξ ∈ I_𝕂, where w_ξ records the jump of the lattice 𝔮 in the ξ-eigenspace.
items.note: The invariant that plays the role of the CM type of a CM Hodge structure, and the input of the Deligne–Gross statement.

items.name: The Hodge–Pink type lies in I_𝕂^0 (Lemma 7.2.3)
items.statement: Let 𝕳 be a pure 𝕜-Hodge–Pink structure of weight w(𝕳) with full CM by a CM field 𝕂 over 𝕜. Then Φ_𝕳 ∈ I_𝕂^0 with wt(Φ_𝕳) = [𝕂:𝕂^+]·w(𝕳).
items.note: This is what makes the period distribution applicable to Φ_𝕳 and so is the step that connects §7 with §3.

items.name: A CM Hodge–Pink substructure comes from a CM dual t-motive
items.statement: Let 𝕄 be a pure uniformizable dual t-motive of weight w(𝕄) over C_∞ and 𝕳' a 𝕜-Hodge–Pink sub-structure of 𝕳(𝕄) with full CM by a CM field 𝕂 over 𝕜. Then 𝕳' is effective and the 𝕄' of Theorem 7.1.8 may be taken to be a CM dual t-motive with generalized CM type (𝕂,Φ_{𝕳'}); by Theorem 2.4.3(3) it may be taken over k-bar and is unique up to isogeny.
items.locator: Published Proposition 7.2.6 and Remark 7.2.7, pp.890–891; period notation in Definition 7.2.8.
items.note: Independent review: Locator corrected. Nonzero positive-weight effectiveness here must be distinguished from the false unrestricted assertion in Remark 7.2.5 (E20).

items.name: The Deligne–Gross conjecture over function fields (Theorem 7.3.1)
items.statement: Let M be a pure uniformizable dual t-motive over k-bar and H'⊂H(M) a Hodge–Pink substructure with full CM by K⊂K_{n,ℓ}, ℓ≥1. Choose rational ε(x,y) with φ_{K,Φ_H'}=Σ ε(x,y)St(x,y), for x∈n(θ)^{-1}A/A, y∈(q^ℓ−1)^{-1}Z/Z. For ρ∈G_{n,ℓ}, let ω_ρ be a nonzero ν₁∘ρ|K eigendifferential in H'_C∞∩H_dR(M,k-bar), identifying the subspace via the period isomorphism. If γ∈H_Betti(M) and ∫_γω_ρ≠0, then ∫_γω_ρ ~ ∏ Γ-tilde(x,y)^{ε(ρ^{-1}★x,ρ^{-1}★y)}.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 7.3.1, with Remarks 7.3.2 and 7.3.3
items.note: Independent review: Arbitrary C_∞-scaled differentials do not preserve the period class modulo k-bar×. Fixed-level ε existence is gated by E6; explicit ε needs E11.

items.name: Analogue of Gross's period formula (Example 7.3.4)
items.statement: Let E_ρ/k-bar be pure uniformizable of dimension d and rank r, with an O_K-action for a CM field K/𝕜 of degree n dividing r. Put d₀=r/n. The determinant Hodge–Pink structure H_K^{d₀}(E_ρ)=∧_K^{d₀}H(E_ρ) has full CM by K, embeds in ∧_𝕜^{d₀}H(E_ρ), has weight d/n and CM-type weight d/[K⁺:𝕜]. If K⊂K_{nmod,ℓ}, its nonzero algebraic eigenperiods obey item 77.
items.note: Independent review: Restored determinant construction, O_K action and degrees; E19 fixes the integral-closure field. Integral exterior-power comparison still needs a separately checked projectivity/saturation argument.

items.name: Shimura's conjecture over function fields (the transcendence input)
items.statement: For a CM field 𝕂 over 𝕜 Galois and fixed by [𝔊,𝔊_∞], the transcendence degree over k-bar of the field generated by the CM periods p_𝕂(ξ,Φ^0), for Φ^0 ∈ I_𝕂^0, is 1 + (1 - 1/[𝕂:𝕂^+])·[𝕂:𝕜], the dimension of the corresponding Q-vector space of CM types.
items.locator: arXiv:2207.01165v2 (11 January 2026), Theorem 3.3.5, quoted from the main theorem of Brownawell–Chang–Papanikolas–Wei
items.note: Independent review: Duplicate imported CM transcendence input underlying 37. DM.8 gives the general Papanikolas criterion and a Carlitz-log application, explicitly requiring separately proved hypotheses for other periods. BCPW's CM-group calculation is not thereby planned.

items.name: The Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion
items.statement: Let E consist of power series Σa_it^i with a_i∈k-bar, coefficients in a finite extension of k_∞, and lim |a_i|_∞^{1/i}=0. If Φ∈Mat_r(k-bar[t]) has det Φ=c(t−θ)^s, c≠0,s≥0, and ψ∈E^r satisfies ψ^{(−1)}=Φψ, then every row ρ∈k-bar^{1×r} with ρψ(θ)=0 lifts to P∈k-bar[t]^{1×r} with P(θ)=ρ and Pψ=0.
items.locator: ABP (2004), Theorem 1.3.2 (=3.1.1), p.240; background input to Wei via the cited soliton/CM-period works.
items.note: Independent review: Checked primary statement. DM.8 owns lifting, not the special CM conclusion. Share this import with the multiple-zeta Part II proposals.

items.name: Drinfeld 𝔸-modules and CM by an order
items.statement: Over L⊃k, a rank-r Drinfeld F_q[t]-module is determined by ρ_t=θ+a₁τ+⋯+a_rτ^r with a_r≠0 and τc=c^qτ; morphisms commute with ρ. Over C_∞ its uniformization gives an A-lattice of rank r. For an order O in an imaginary degree-r field K/𝕜, CM by O means an F_q[t]-algebra embedding O→End(E_ρ).
items.note: Independent review: Definition and Drinfeld uniformization only, not the CM existence/isogeny/period-symbol theorems. Removed unrelated Tate-module layer.

items.name: Dirichlet characters and L-functions over 𝔸
items.statement: For monic n and ℓ≥1, χ is a complex character of G_{n,ℓ}; cχ is the conductor of its finite part. The primitive Dirichlet L-function is ∏_{monic irreducible p ∤ cχ}(1−χ_f(p)χ_∞(deg p)q^{-s deg p})^{-1} for Re(s)>1, with meromorphic continuation and value/derivative at 0. For cχ|m, the imprimitive L_A^m removes additionally the factors for p|m,p∤cχ.
items.note: Independent review: FA.5 finite-cover Artin-factor scope. Conductor and constant-field Frobenius are explicit; do not replace L_A^m by L_A in evaluator formulas.

items.name: Transcendence degree of a field extension
items.statement: trdeg_F E for a field extension E/F, used throughout to state the main theorem.
items.note: Independent review: Read exact statements at 082e2d3. Algebra.trdeg is cardinal-valued; finite dimension comparisons need cardinal/natural coercions. Finite basis theorem requires FinTrdeg.

items.name: Locally constant functions and the Haar measure of a profinite group
items.statement: Locally constant Q-valued functions on a profinite group, and the normalised Haar measure used to state condition (2) of Definition 3.2.1.
items.note: Independent review: Read all declarations at 082e2d3. haarMeasure takes K₀:PositiveCompacts; choose univ for compact G and use haarMeasure_self. Q-valued averages are rational finite-quotient sums, or real integrals after coercion, not a Bochner integral with target Q.

items.name: The normed field C_∞ and chosen algebraic closure of k
items.statement: Construct k_∞ at infinity with |θ|=q, extend the norm to an algebraic closure and complete to C_∞; fix k-bar as the algebraic closure of k inside it. Record completeness, nonarchimedean norm, characteristic p and algebraic closedness.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 1. Reviewed DM.2 audit explicitly leaves rank-one normalization and positive-characteristic completion algebraic closedness missing. Planned does not mean built; import general valuations/completions.

items.name: Arithmetic gamma values with denominator q−1
items.statement: For 0≤a<q−1 integral, Γ_ari(1−a/(q−1))~π-tilde^{a/(q−1)}.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 5; not supplied by the Carlitz period lattice. The case a=q−1 is not included; do not use this to identify Γ_ari(0) with 1.

items.name: Restricted-series carrier for the one-variable Tate algebra
items.statement: Over a complete nonarchimedean normed field C, the restricted-series subring in one variable consists of formal series with coefficients tending to zero. Use MvPowerSeries at one variable and radius 1; identify multi-indices Fin 1→₀N with N for the paper's notation.
items.note: Independent review: Read declarations at pins. This is the carrier, not a claim that twists, dagger analytic continuation, Betti module or period evaluation are already implemented. Reuse upstream AdicSpaces.

items.name: Dagger analytic continuation and evaluation of Betti cycles
items.statement: For a uniformizable dual t-motive M, the Betti cycles extend from T⊗M to T†⊗M, with T† the subring of rigid analytic functions on C_∞ minus {θ^{q^i}:i≥1}; evaluation at θ gives the de Rham period pairing.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 19. Exact analytic domain/continuation proof and comparison maps must be separate leaves; imported carrier 87 is insufficient.

items.name: Hartl–Juschka dual and quasi-period comparison
items.statement: For abelian E_ρ, let M_ρ=Hom_Fq(E_ρ,G_a). Its Hartl–Juschka dual is Hom_{k-bar[t]}(τM_ρ,k-bar[t]dt) with the specified inverse-Frobenius action. Under the de Rham and lattice/Betti comparison isomorphisms of (6.1.2), the t-module pairing [δ,λ] corresponds to minus the dual-motive pairing ∫_γω.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 60. The σ action and both comparison isomorphisms need atomic extraction from BCPW/Hartl–Juschka/Namoijam–Papanikolas. DM.2 is Drinfeld-only; DM.4 owns the τ-motive input.

items.name: Quotient-normalized gamma values
items.statement: For y∈Z_(p)/Z, Γ-tilde_ari(y)=Γ_ari(1−⟨−y⟩_ari). For x∈k/A, Γ-tilde(x,y)=Γ({x},1−⟨−y⟩_ari) if x≠0, and Γ-tilde_ari(y)^{-1} if x=0. Define Γ-tilde_geo independently as Γ_ari(1−1/(q−1))^{-1} times Γ_geo({x}) if x≠0, or 1 if x=0. Composing rational products with C_∞×→C_∞×/k-bar× gives the hat maps.
items.note: Independent review: Previously absent definition of the central target. E7 forbids equating the last piecewise definition with Γ-tilde(x,1/(1−q)) at q=2. Rational powers are canonical only after quotienting; arbitrary lift choices differ algebraically.

items.name: Compatible separable-closure and decomposition-subgroup choices
items.statement: Fix 𝕜^sep and an embedding ν:𝕜^sep→k-bar extending v_θ. The chosen extension of the infinite valuation gives a decomposition subgroup G_∞ of G=Gal(𝕜^sep/𝕜), identified with the corresponding absolute local Galois group; restriction must be compatible across finite subextensions.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 7. Import FA.3 finite decomposition groups and general profinite Galois theory; do not re-plan them in the proposed Part II. Exact assembly owner/bridge remains a route-1 gap.

items.name: Restricting the period distribution to the Carlitz tower
items.statement: For K^cyc the compositum of Carlitz cyclotomic and constant extensions, S(G^cyc) is the subspace of S(G) factoring through G^cyc=Gal(K^cyc/𝕜); P^cyc_ν is the restriction of P_ν to this subspace.
items.note: Independent review: Split from 38: this is CM-period-distribution theory, not generic FA.4 reciprocity.

items.name: Gamma normalization for the Lerch formula
items.statement: For y=Σy_iq^i∈Z_p put ∂(y)=Σiy_iq^i. For rational y∈Z_(p), set Γ*_ari(y)=θ^{∂(y−1)}Γ_ari(y), with a consistent rational-power interpretation. For nonzero admissible x∈k put ∂(x,y)=⟨x,−y⟩ and Γ*(x,y)=x^{1−∂(x,y−1)}θ^{−∂(y−1)}Γ(x,y). Define Γ*(0,y)=Γ*_ari(y)^{-1} separately.
items.note: Independent review: The original extraction used Γ* without defining it. E21 corrects the arity typo; zero is a separate extension, not evaluation of x^{1−∂}Γ(x,y). Local logarithmic normalization requires explicit absolute-value handling.

prerequisites.citation: W. D. Brownawell, C.-Y. Chang, M. A. Papanikolas and F.-T. Wei, "Function field analogue of Shimura's conjecture on period symbols"
prerequisites.why: The transcendence input of the whole paper: the computation of the transcendence degree of the field generated by the CM period symbols of a CM field over 𝕜, which is quoted as Theorem 3.3.5. It also supplies the period symbols themselves (its §5), their functoriality and Legendre relation (its Theorem 5.3.2), the geometric definition of CM dual t-motives and the existence and isogeny statements of Theorem 2.4.3.

prerequisites.citation: D. S. Thakur, "Gamma functions for function fields and Drinfeld modules", Annals of Mathematics (2) 134 (1991), 25–64
prerequisites.why: The geometric and two-variable gamma functions with their functional equations, the diamond brackets of §4.1, and the conjectured Chowla–Selberg recipe of its 7.12 that Theorem 6.2.3 proves.

prerequisites.citation: D. Goss, "The Γ-function in the arithmetic of function fields", Duke Mathematical Journal 56 (1988), 163–191
prerequisites.why: The original two-variable gamma function, compared with Thakur's normalisation in Remark 5.4.1, and the interpolation theory the three gamma functions rest on.

prerequisites.citation: G. W. Anderson, W. D. Brownawell and M. A. Papanikolas, "Determination of the algebraic relations among special Γ-values in positive characteristic", Annals of Mathematics (2) 160 (2004), 237–313
prerequisites.why: The geometric case of the main theorem, the linear independence criterion used throughout, the shtuka functions of §6.3.9 quoted as Theorem 5.2.1, and the soliton construction of its 6.4.2 that §5.3 generalizes to two variables.

prerequisites.citation: M. A. Papanikolas, "Tannakian duality for Anderson–Drinfeld motives and algebraic independence of Carlitz logarithms", Inventiones mathematicae 171 (2008), 123–174
prerequisites.why: The Tannakian and Frobenius-difference-Galois theory that computes transcendence degrees of periods of dual t-motives, on which the Shimura-conjecture input rests. DM.8 already names it as its source, so it is listed here for the record rather than as a new acquisition.

prerequisites.citation: U. Hartl and A.-K. Juschka, "Pink's theory of Hodge structures and the Hodge conjecture over function fields", in t-Motives: Hodge Structures, Transcendence and Other Motivic Aspects, EMS, Zürich, 2020, 31–182
prerequisites.why: Mixed 𝕜-Hodge–Pink structures with their weight filtration and lattice, the local semistable condition, purity of dual t-motives and the containment of the Betti module in T^† ⊗ 𝕄; §7 is written entirely in this language.

prerequisites.citation: G. W. Anderson, "Logarithmic derivatives of Dirichlet L-functions and the periods of abelian varieties", Compositio Mathematica 45 (1982), 315–332
prerequisites.why: The classical period distribution and the theorem of Deligne stated as its Theorem 4.7, of which Theorem 5.4.5 is the function-field analogue; also the model for the logarithmic form of the Chowla–Selberg formula in §6.4.

prerequisites.citation: C.-Y. Chang, M. A. Papanikolas, D. S. Thakur and J. Yu, "Algebraic independence of arithmetic gamma values and Carlitz zeta values", Advances in Mathematics 223 (2010), 1137–1154
prerequisites.why: The arithmetic case of the main theorem, recovered by taking 𝔫 = 1, and the transcendence techniques for arithmetic gamma values.

prerequisites.citation: D. S. Kubert and S. Lang, "Modular units", Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 244, Springer, 1981
prerequisites.why: The theory of distributions and universal distributions, in the sense of its Chapter 1 §3, which §4.3 uses to show that the three Stickelberger distributions are universal.

prerequisites.citation: G. W. Anderson, "t-motives", Duke Mathematical Journal 53 (1986), 457–502
prerequisites.why: Abelian t-modules and their motives, the objects whose quasi-periods the Chowla–Selberg formula of §6 computes. DM.4 already names it as its source.

prerequisites.citation: F.-T. Wei, On Kronecker terms over global function fields, Invent. Math. 220 (2020), 847–907
prerequisites.why: Wei §6.4 uses its Kronecker limit formula (5.3) for analytic Chowla–Selberg and stable Taguchi-height consequences. Acquire/check exact source before treating these as extracted.

prerequisites.citation: C. Namoijam and M. A. Papanikolas, Hyperderivatives of periods and quasi-periods for Anderson t-modules
prerequisites.why: §6.1 imports its de Rham module and pairing, including the comparison conventions; absent from original prerequisite list. Source not read in full here.

routes.brief: WITHHELD BY REV-PAPER-WEI-26: this is a candidate direction, not an accepted design specification. The intended exact targets are item 8 (the published trdeg formula), item 10 (the period distribution), corrected items 11/90 (three gamma distributions), items 14/61/62 (the ideal-parametrized lattice and the full Galois orbit of quasi-periods), the still incomplete three-part item 65, and item 77 (nonzero algebraic CM eigenperiods, not arbitrary periods). Repair source findings E5–E13/E18 before activating boundary-sensitive proofs; do not infer the main trdeg formula is false. Complete the gaps ledger in REV-PAPER-WEI-26.md, splitting formulas and proof prerequisites. Import Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values (DrinfeldModulesAndTModules) DM.0/DM.2 for Carlitz and Drinfeld uniformization, DM.4 for τ-motives/purity, DM.8 for the precise ABP/Papanikolas machinery; construct the σ-dual comparison, not a duplicated general theory. Import Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), FA.3/FA.4/FA.5, for finite ramification, reciprocity comparisons and Artin factors. Reuse the pinned Tate carrier and upstream Adic spaces (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces) rather than rebuilding it. The proposed multiple-zeta DrinfeldModulesAndTModulesPartII shares ABP and dual-motive foundations, so resolve shared ownership before any new design. Classical Hodge structures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures) does not supply Hodge–Pink structures. BCPW's specific CM group calculation is an additional input, not a consequence supplied by the generic DM.8 layer. The candidate route presently holds unsolved assemblies solely to preserve single routing; that is not an ownership endorsement.

Narrowed source route: 5 and 85 supply the Carlitz period and its analytic ambient field (DM.0/DM.2); 60 supplies the abelian τ-motive convention (DM.4); 80 is the actual ABP lifting criterion (DM.8); 81 supplies Drinfeld-module/uniformization definitions (DM.0/DM.2).
